column3: Human vocal fold cover (epithelium and superficial layer of the lamina propria) separated from the ligament by blunt dissection, from seven subjects, all nonsmokers with normal true folds, kept in PBS (pH 7.4) at room temperature before testing; subject 1: female, 53 y, African American, 3 h after total laryngectomy; subject 2: female, 58 y, Hispanic, 4 h after total laryngectomy; subject 3: male, 60 y, Caucasian, 9 h postmortem; subject 4: male, 64 y, Caucasian, 15 h postmortem; subject 5: male, 69 y, Caucasian, 20 h postmortem; subject 6: male, 79 y, Caucasian, 11 h postmortem; subject 7: male, 88 y, Caucasian, 10 h postmortem. The source's footnote: postmortem time is the time from death to rheometry, except subjects 1 and 2 who were total laryngectomy patients
column4: Controlled-strain linear SIMPLE-SHEAR rheometer: the specimen between two rigid parallel acrylic plates (nominal gap 1.0 mm), sinusoidal displacement of the upper plate by a linear motor (0.01 mm amplitude = 1.0 percent shear strain), force on the lower plate by a piezoelectric transducer, displacement by an LVDT, at least 20 cycles per frequency, frequency sweep 1-250 Hz (the range the authors validated against a standard polyurethane, ANSI S2.21), environmental chamber with ambient air about 37 C and relative humidity near 100 percent; strain sweep at 100 Hz: G' constant up to a strain amplitude of about 3-7 percent
column5: Power laws are fitted to the MEAN of the seven specimens (not per specimen) over 1-250 Hz and must not be extrapolated. The source defines the damping ratio as the ratio of the viscous to the elastic modulus (loss factor G''/G'), not c/(2 sqrt(km)). Below about 50 Hz G'' exceeds G' (liquid-like terminal region), unlike earlier torsional studies; above it G' exceeds G''. The units printed for the coefficient p are Pa.s (G', G'') and Pa.s2 (eta'): p is the value at f = 1 Hz in Pa (Pa.s for eta') with f in Hz, so it is stored dimensionless with the unit in the property name. The exponent of eta' is negative in the source (shear thinning); its magnitude is stored. Cadaveric and laryngectomy tissue of 53-88 y subjects; n = 7. Standard deviations are printed only in a figure and are not recorded

column3: The printed power laws evaluated at two phonatory frequencies (COMPUTED here from the printed p and q, not printed in the source)
column4: G'(f) = p f^q and G''(f) = p f^q with the printed coefficients, f in Hz, result in Pa
column5: Derived values, valid only inside 1-250 Hz; they inherit every caveat of the fit to the seven-specimen mean
